course.title: IELTS Starter: Everyday Topics
course.description: Band 4.0–5.0. Familiar topics, IELTS question types and short answers, written for IeltsWithHarry.

lessons.title: Health, illness and staying well
lessons.summary: Words for common illnesses, healthy habits and relaxing.

material.introduction:
Health is a frequent topic in IELTS Reading passages and in Writing Task 2 questions about lifestyle. Learn words for common problems (a headache, stress) and healthy habits (get enough sleep, cut down on sugar), then use them to give advice.

Mẹo: have a headache / have a cold / feel stressed – chú ý động từ đi kèm.

vocabulary.definition: To feel pain in your head.
vocabulary.example: I often have a headache if I don't drink enough water.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Tôi bị đau đầu sau giờ học.
acceptedSentences: I have a headache after class.
I had a headache after class.
I have a headache after school.

vocabulary.definition: To become ill with a mild illness that affects your nose and throat.
vocabulary.example: Wear a jacket or you'll catch a cold.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Em gái tôi bị cảm lạnh tuần trước.
acceptedSentences: My sister caught a cold last week.
My younger sister caught a cold last week.

vocabulary.definition: A feeling of worry caused by difficult situations.
vocabulary.example: Exams cause a lot of stress for students.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Thể dục giúp giảm căng thẳng.

vocabulary.definition: To sleep for as long as your body needs.
vocabulary.example: Teenagers need to get enough sleep to concentrate.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Tôi không ngủ đủ giấc.
acceptedSentences: I do not get enough sleep.

vocabulary.definition: To have or do less of something.
vocabulary.example: My doctor told me to cut down on sugar.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Tôi nên cắt giảm đồ ăn nhanh.
acceptedSentences: I should cut down on fast food.
I need to cut down on fast food.

vocabulary.definition: To do physical exercise, usually in a gym.
vocabulary.example: He works out three times a week.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Tôi tập thể dục ở phòng gym.
acceptedSentences: I work out at the gym.
I work out in the gym.

vocabulary.definition: A doctor's written instruction for medicine.
vocabulary.example: You need a prescription to buy this medicine.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Bác sĩ đưa cho tôi một đơn thuốc.
acceptedSentences: The doctor gave me a prescription.

vocabulary.definition: Time spent looking at phones, computers or TVs.
vocabulary.example: Too much screen time before bed affects your sleep.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Tôi muốn giảm thời gian dùng màn hình.
acceptedSentences: I want to reduce my screen time.
I want to cut down on screen time.
I want to reduce screen time.

lessons.title: Should, have to and don't have to
lessons.summary: Give advice and talk about rules and necessity.

material.rule:
should / shouldn't + base verb – advice: You should drink more water. You shouldn't skip breakfast.
have to / has to + base verb – something is necessary or a rule: Nurses have to work at night. She has to take this medicine twice a day.
don't / doesn't have to – it is NOT necessary (you can choose): You don't have to make an appointment; just come in.
mustn't – it is not allowed: You mustn't smoke in the hospital.

Cẩn thận: don't have to (không cần) ≠ mustn't (không được phép).
material.example: You don't have to go to a gym to stay fit, but you should walk at least thirty minutes a day.

questions.prompt: You look tired. You ___ go to bed earlier.
In this clinic, patients ___ wear a mask. It's a rule.
questions.explanation: Quy định bắt buộc → have to.

questions.prompt: It's free – you ___ pay for the health check.
questions.explanation: Không cần thiết phải trả tiền → don't have to.

questions.prompt: My father ___ take his medicine every morning.
questions.explanation: Chủ ngữ số ít 'My father' → has to.

questions.prompt: You ___ use your phone in the operating room. It's not allowed.

options: You should to eat more fruit.
questions.explanation: should + động từ nguyên mẫu, không 'to'.

lessons.title: Do students sleep enough?
lessons.summary: Read an opinion essay and identify the writer's views.

material.passage:
Many people believe that teenagers are simply lazy when they find it hard to get up in the morning. In my opinion, this view is unfair, and schools should do more to help students sleep well.

First of all, the body clock changes during the teenage years. Research shows that most teenagers naturally feel sleepy later at night than children or adults do. If they must be at school by seven, many of them cannot get the eight to ten hours of sleep that doctors recommend.

Secondly, students today have more reasons to stay awake. Homework, extra classes and social media all compete for the evening hours. Bright screens also send a signal to the brain that it is still daytime, which makes it harder to fall asleep.

The effects of too little sleep are serious. Tired students find it difficult to concentrate, and they are more likely to feel stressed or anxious. Some studies have also found that they are more likely to have accidents on the way to school.

Some people argue that a later start time would cause problems for parents who work early. This is a fair point, but schools could offer a supervised study room for students who arrive early.

In conclusion, I believe that later school start times, less homework at weekends and lessons about healthy sleep habits would make a real difference to students' health and results.

questions.prompt: What is the writer's opinion about the belief that teenagers are lazy?
questions.explanation: 'In my opinion, this view is unfair'.
questions.evidence: In my opinion, this view is unfair

questions.prompt: According to the essay, why do teenagers feel sleepy later at night?
questions.explanation: 'the body clock changes during the teenage years'.
questions.evidence: the body clock changes during the teenage years

questions.prompt: How do bright screens affect sleep?
options: They tell the brain it is still daytime.
questions.explanation: Màn hình sáng 'send a signal to the brain that it is still daytime'.
questions.evidence: send a signal to the brain that it is still daytime

questions.prompt: Tired students are more likely to have accidents on the way to school. (True / False / Not Given)
questions.explanation: 'they are more likely to have accidents on the way to school' → True.
questions.evidence: they are more likely to have accidents on the way to school

questions.prompt: How does the writer answer the problem for working parents?
options: Schools could open a supervised study room.
questions.explanation: 'schools could offer a supervised study room for students who arrive early'.
questions.evidence: schools could offer a supervised study room for students who arrive early

questions.prompt: Which is NOT one of the writer's suggestions in the conclusion?
questions.explanation: Kết luận đề xuất giờ học muộn hơn, ít bài tập cuối tuần và bài học về giấc ngủ – không nhắc cấm điện thoại.
questions.evidence: later school start times, less homework at weekends and lessons about healthy sleep habits

lessons.title: Staying active at work
lessons.summary: Listen to a radio interview and answer multiple-choice questions.

material.transcript:
Presenter: Today we're talking about office workers who sit at a desk all day. With me is physiotherapist Dr Kate Lim. Kate, how long do most office workers sit each day?
Kate: In our survey, the average was nine hours, including the time at home in the evening. That's a lot more than people expect.
Presenter: Why is that a problem?
Kate: Sitting for a long time without moving is bad for your back and neck, and it slows down your body's use of energy. Even people who go to the gym can be affected if they sit all day.
Presenter: So what should people do?
Kate: The simplest thing is to stand up every thirty minutes. You don't have to do exercises – just walk to get some water or stretch your arms.
Presenter: Many listeners say they don't exercise because it takes too much time.
Kate: Yes, that's the most common reason people give, more than the cost. But a ten-minute walk at lunchtime really helps. I spend twenty minutes outside on my lunch break, and I feel much more awake in the afternoon.
Presenter: Any final advice?
Kate: Take the stairs instead of the lift. It's free, and it's a good workout for your legs.

questions.prompt: According to the survey, how many hours a day do office workers sit on average?
What does Kate say about people who go to the gym?
options: They can still be affected by sitting all day.
questions.explanation: 'Even people who go to the gym can be affected if they sit all day.'

questions.prompt: How often should office workers stand up?
What is the most common reason people give for not exercising?
questions.explanation: 'that's the most common reason people give, more than the cost'.

questions.prompt: How long does Kate spend outside on her lunch break?
questions.explanation: Cô ấy dành 20 phút; 10 phút là thời gian đi bộ cô khuyên người nghe – dễ nhầm.

lessons.title: An email giving health advice
lessons.summary: Write a 100–120 word email to a friend who feels stressed.

material.prompt: Your friend Nam wrote to you: 'I've got exams next month and I feel stressed all the time. I can't sleep well and I eat lots of junk food. What should I do?' Write an email to Nam (100–120 words). Give at least three pieces of advice and explain why each one will help. Use should, shouldn't and don't have to.
material.modelAnswer:
Hi Nam,

I'm sorry to hear you're feeling stressed. Here are a few ideas that helped me last year.

First, you should make a study timetable. When you know exactly what to revise each day, the exams feel less frightening. Second, you shouldn't use your phone in bed, because the bright screen makes it harder to fall asleep. Try reading a book instead. Third, you don't have to give up snacks completely, but you should cut down on crisps and sweets and eat more fruit. Healthy food gives you more energy for studying.

Finally, take short breaks and go for a walk. Fresh air really clears your mind.

Good luck!
An
checklist: Respond to your friend's problem in the first line
Give at least three pieces of advice
Explain why each piece of advice helps
Use should, shouldn't and don't have to correctly

lessons.title: Talking about a healthy lifestyle
lessons.summary: Answer Part 1 questions about health and relaxing.

material.prompt:
IELTS Speaking Part 1 – answer each question in 2–3 sentences:
1. What do you do to stay healthy?
2. How do you usually relax after a busy day?
3. Do you think young people in your country get enough exercise?
4. What advice would you give to someone who wants to sleep better?
material.modelAnswer: I try to walk to college instead of taking the bus, and I play football with my friends on Sunday mornings. After a busy day I usually relax by listening to music or chatting with my family over dinner. Honestly, I don't think young people get enough exercise, because they spend so much time on their phones. I'd say you should stop using screens an hour before bed and try to go to sleep at the same time every night.
checklist: Use health vocabulary from this unit
Use should for advice in question 4
Give your opinion with 'I think' or 'Honestly'
Listen again: did you speak for at least 15 seconds each time?
